title: Drupal release metadata can attach the literal "Insecure" Release type term to a core release row
summary: SOURCE FACT: the Drupal update-status release-history feed can attach a Release type taxonomy term whose literal value is "Insecure" to an individual Drupal core release row. PROJECT JOIN: a future finding evaluator may match this only when the Project Analyzer observed installed Drupal core version matches that exact release row in the canonical reviewed release lifecycle context. DRUPAL SEMANTICS (reviewed): For Drupal Update Manager release metadata, a release carrying Release type "Insecure" is treated as insecure; when that exact release is installed, Drupal assigns NOT_SECURE status, whose documented meaning is that the project is missing security update(s). LIMITS: this reviewed meaning does not establish an exploit path, a specific CVE identifier, a finding severity level, or any compromise claim about a project.

Confirmation stays bound to these references, never a status flip.
